subsystems.name: Spacecraft bus and power
subsystems.role: the structural frame and the nuclear power source that must run for decades far from the Sun.

subsystems.name: Science instruments
subsystems.role: remote sensing of a small, fast-moving target in a few hours.

subsystems.name: Communications
subsystems.role: gets the stored data back across billions of kilometres.
parts: X-band transmitter and travelling-wave tube amplifier

subsystems.name: Attitude control and navigation
subsystems.role: points the camera and steers toward a target that is only a dot until the last weeks.
parts: star trackers and inertial measurement units

subsystems.name: Thermal control
subsystems.role: keeps electronics near room temperature in an environment close to absolute zero.

subsystems.name: Propulsion
subsystems.role: small course corrections during a decade-long coast.

buildSteps.title: Find a reachable target
buildSteps.detail: Ground and space telescopes (including Hubble) survey the Kuiper Belt to find a body lying close to the spacecraft's path, so that only a small course correction is needed.

buildSteps.title: Design a one-shot spacecraft
buildSteps.detail: A flyby gives no second chance, so every instrument must work first time; the design centres on an RTG, a fixed dish and a large solid-state recorder.

buildSteps.title: Build and test the payload
buildSteps.detail: A long-focal-length telescope, imaging spectrometers, a radio science package and dust and plasma sensors are assembled and shaken and baked in thermal-vacuum chambers.

buildSteps.title: Launch and gain speed
buildSteps.detail: A heavy launch vehicle sends the probe onto a solar-system escape trajectory, and a flyby of Jupiter provides a gravity assist that cuts years off the cruise.

buildSteps.title: Cruise for years
buildSteps.detail: The craft coasts in electronic hibernation, waking periodically for checkouts, while the Deep Space Network tracks it and refines its path.

buildSteps.title: Retarget with optical navigation
buildSteps.detail: Months out, the camera begins imaging the target against background stars; tiny hydrazine burns steer the spacecraft to within a few thousand kilometres.

buildSteps.title: Fly by in hours
buildSteps.detail: A pre-loaded command sequence runs autonomously: approach imaging, closest approach, high-phase and low-phase views, all written to the recorder as the craft races past at about 14 km/s.

buildSteps.title: Downlink and analyse
buildSteps.detail: Data trickle back at a few kilobits per second for many months, then are calibrated, archived and compared with other primitive bodies.

prerequisites.why: sunlight is too faint beyond Jupiter for solar panels; plutonium-238 production is limited, so fuel supply is a real constraint.
only very large dishes can hear a few-watt signal from over 40 AU, and the downlink takes months.
a 30 km object must be resolved from millions of kilometres away during a brief encounter.

prerequisites.tech: Ground and space-based Kuiper Belt surveys
prerequisites.why: targets are tiny and faint, so a flyby is only possible if one is found on or near the trajectory years in advance.

prerequisites.tech: Low-temperature electronics and autonomous fault protection
prerequisites.why: the probe operates near -230 °C for much of its life, with heaters and hibernation keeping systems alive without ground control.

pathway.milestone: New Horizons continues its extended mission after the 2019 Arrokoth flyby
pathway.unlocks: ongoing measurements of the outer heliosphere and Kuiper Belt dust.

pathway.milestone: dedicated Kuiper Belt flyby mission concepts studied by space agencies
pathway.unlocks: a second look at a different dynamical class of object, with modern instruments.

pathway.milestone: faster trajectories using current heavy-lift launchers
pathway.unlocks: encounters within a decade rather than two, and possibly more than one target.

pathway.milestone: a Kuiper Belt rendezvous using nuclear electric propulsion
pathway.unlocks: orbital study and mapping instead of a fleeting flyby, though still a multi-decade undertaking.
